column1: # Negative claims about the Canonical ABI reference (`definitions.py`), one row per claim in an accepted ADR.
# A negative claim ("the reference does not…", "only…", "never…") names no symbol, so `make refcite` cannot see it
# rot. ADR 0100's no-poison premise was true at 2bed77e and false at 2e7895c, and nothing fired (#1040). So this
# list is the population a pin move must re-read, by the chair's third ruling of 2026-10-20.
# THE PIN-MOVE RULE: after moving CANON_PIN, re-read every row below at the new pin, then set its read_at to the
# new pin. `make refcite` fails until every row's read_at equals CANON_PIN. A row whose claim has become false
# gets `false` and the number of the issue that owns it.
# `make refcite` checks that the list is kept: each quote still appears in its ADR, each read_at is the current
# pin, and each `false` row names an issue. It cannot find a negative claim nobody listed. Adding a row when an
# ADR makes a new claim about the reference is the author's job, and the sweep of 2026-10-20 (#1040) is the
# One row per claim, tab-separated: the ADR number, a verbatim quote of the claim (whitespace-insensitive, no
# tab), read_at (the full pin SHA it was last re-read at), the verdict (holds or false), the issue (a number, or
# - when it holds), and a note.
